label: Java
note: The Java logo is an Oracle trademark and is not redistributable. We use the OpenJDK mark — the reference implementation — which Java developers recognise.

label: S3
note: AWS does not redistribute its marks under a free licence. The “bucket” pictogram borrows S3's own vocabulary, which its users recognise.

label: Tomcat
note: A weak case, knowingly kept: the brand colour is very light (#F8DC75), which forces a desaturated ink, and the logo is a delicate line drawing. It clears the contrast threshold (4.9:1) but stays the least legible mark of the set at small sizes. Prefer the stacked layout, which is larger.

label: RabbitMQ
note: Ruled out as a protocol sign by ADR 0002 — RabbitMQ is not AMQP, WireGuard is not “VPN”. As a product, the logo is perfectly legitimate again.

label: WireGuard
note: Ruled out as a protocol sign by ADR 0002 — RabbitMQ is not AMQP, WireGuard is not “VPN”. As a product, the logo is perfectly legitimate again.

label: MinIO
note: S3-compatible object storage you can install on premises: the local counterpart to S3, useful when the diagram does not describe a public cloud.

label: Google Cloud
note: The only major cloud provider whose mark is in Simple Icons: AWS and Azure were removed from it for trademark reasons. For those, use the generic “cloud provider” role.

label: Cloud provider
note: AWS and Azure were removed from Simple Icons for trademark reasons: this role designates them without naming them, and the box label says which one.
